title: 2018 AMC 10B Problem 17
statement: In rectangle \(PQRS,\) \(PQ = 8\) and \(QR = 6.\) Points \(A\) and \(B\) lie on \(PQ,\) points \(C\) and \(D\) lie on \(QR,\) points \(E\) and \(F\) lie on \(RS,\) and points \(G\) and \(H\) lie on \(SP\) so that \(AP = BQ < 4\) and the convex octagon \(ABCDEFGH\) is equilateral. The length of a side of this octagon can be expressed in the form \(k + m\sqrt{n},\) where \(k,\) \(m,\) and \(n\) are integers and \(n\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(k + m + n?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(s\) be the octagon’s side length and let \(x=AP=BQ=\frac{8-s}{2}.\) The right triangles \(\triangle APH\) and \(\triangle BQC\) have the same hypotenuse \(s\) and a leg of length \(x,\) so they are congruent; write \(PH=QC=y.\) Because \(CD=HG=s\) and the vertical sides of the rectangle both have length \(6,\) it follows that \(DR=GS.\) The right triangles at \(R\) and \(S\) are then congruent, so \(RE=SF.\) Since \(RS=8\) and \(EF=s,\) each of these equal lengths is \(\frac{8-s}{2}=x.\) Thus all four cut corners have legs \(x\) and \(y.\)

The equal octagon sides give \[8-2x=6-2y=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}.\] The first equality gives \(y=x-1.\) Substituting and squaring gives \(2x^2-30x+63=0,\) so the root with \(x<4\) is \(x=\frac{15-3\sqrt{11}}{2}.\)

The side length is \(8-2x=-7+3\sqrt{11},\) so \(k+m+n=-7+3+11=7.\) Thus, B is the correct answer.
